Archeology uncovers the ways people lived in the past through the places and artifacts they left behind. The stories revealed by archeologists bring a unique perspective to the present and to our choices about the future. Are you curious about how people in other times and places met the challenges they faced? Do you enjoy putting clues together to solve mysteries? Archeology just might be for you! Explore this website to learn about what archeologists do, and what you can do to help the National Park Service preserve and protect archeological resources for this and future generations. People Learn from other people's perspectives. Places Explore the lands and waters where people left a mark. Artifacts See how material things evidence the past. Search Twitter YouTube Facebook Instagram Flickr LinkedIn Arctic District Arctic District lands comprise 23.1 million acres of public lands north of the Brooks Range. Lands primarily include the National Petroleum Reserve in Alaska, which is the largest contiguous block of federal land managed by a single agency. The petroleum reserve provides for significant oil and gas exploration and development activities, important habitat for migratory birds and caribou, and subsistence hunting and fishing access for rural residents. View Arctic District Boundary Map A critically important national resource, the lands are managed by the Alaska State Office, Division of Resources, in Anchorage. A limited number of resource program specialists are also co-located with Fairbanks District staff in Fairbanks. The district's priority is to provide for the energy needs of the nation while protecting the environment and subsistence resources that are critically important to the people of the North Slope. The district is currently engaged in several land use plans and environmental impact statements related to oil and gas leasing and development in the Alaskan Arctic. pages.description: art002e009301 (April 6, 2026) – Captured by the Artemis II crew during their lunar flyby on April 6, 2026, this image shows the Moon fully eclipsing the Sun. pages.description: NASA is targeting the first Artemis lunar landing in early 2028. After launching the crew aboard the Orion spacecraft, they will transfer to a commercial lunar lander for transport to the surface of the Moon. Lander readiness will determine which provider will safely carry them to the surface and back to Orion in lunar orbit before the crew returns home aboard Orion—splashing down safely in the Pacific Ocean.

Secretary of the Treasury Alexander Hamilton stepped forward with a plan to establish a national bank—which still stands in Independence National Historical Park—that would give the federal government more authority to handle the fiscal situation. His proposal incited a debate that tested the US Constitution’s boundaries and laid the foundation for the country’s financial system. Since then, banking, lending money, and printing currency have continued to grow and fluctuate and entrepreneurial Americans, such as Maggie Walker , have led the banking world to new heights. They are an essential part of American history and embody the strong and resilient characteristics of the American people - so much so that they were designated as our National Mammal in 2016. Once numbering ~30 million and ranging across the United States and in Canada and Mexico, bison were hunted to near extinction, with only several hundred remaining by the 1870’s. What are the three branches of government? The Constitution of the United States divides the federal government into three branches: Legislative Judicial Executive This ensures that no individual or group will have too much power. Legislative branch The legislative branch is made up of Congress : The U.S. Senate The U.S. House of Representatives It also includes special agencies and offices that provide support services to Congress. The legislative branch’s key roles include: Drafting proposed laws Confirming or rejecting presidential nominations for heads of federal agencies, federal judges, and the Supreme Court Surveying the budget Having the authority to declare war Judicial branch The judicial branch includes the Supreme Court and other federal courts. It evaluates laws by: Interpreting the meaning of laws Applying laws to individual cases Deciding if laws violate the Constitution Executive branch The president, the vice president, and the president's cabinet are the members of the executive branch. The executive branch’s key roles include: The president is the head of state, leader of the executive branch, and commander in chief of the United States armed forces. The vice president supports the president. If the president is unable to serve, the vice president becomes president.
